Born in Adams County, Pennsylvania, 31 January 1818.
He married Eliza Polly, daughter of Daniel Polly, on 18 August 1840.
In 1850 he was living in Cumberland Township, outside Gettysburg, with Eliza and six children;
one of them was Ann, aged eight, who later married into the Wintrodes.
Eliza died in 1856, and he married Mary Lucinda Biesecker.
He farmed rented land south of Gettysburg, and in the fall of 1862 he sowed winter wheat there.
He moved off in the spring of 1863, meaning to come back for the harvest, but on 2 July the battle swept across his
ripening crop, the field known ever since as the Wheatfield, “the scene of some of the bitterest fighting,”
as his daughter Rachel’s obituary put it.
In the 1860 census the household was still in Cumberland Township: Francis, his second wife Lucinda,
Ann, Charles, Jane, Rachel, John, William and the baby Robert.
Charles, his eldest son, enlisted at Gettysburg in August 1862 in Company B of the 138th Pennsylvania Infantry and
was killed at the Battle of Locust Grove (Payne’s Farm) , Virginia, on 27 November 1863,
in the Mine Run campaign. In 1889 Francis applied for a father’s pension on Charles’s service,
and it was granted. In later years he farmed in Franklin Township, near McKnightstown.
He died at Gettysburg on 27 June 1894 and is buried in Evergreen Cemetery.
Eliza Polly was the daughter of Daniel Polly, a Cumberland Township farmer near Gettysburg who was later a township
supervisor. She married Francis C. Ogden on 18 August 1840; the Reverend Samuel Gutelius married them.
In 1850 they were living in Cumberland Township with six children, and that May they buried an eight-month-old son,
Daniel. She died after a long illness in April 1856, about 38, and is buried in Evergreen Cemetery,
Gettysburg. Their daughter Ann married into the Wintrodes.
